summary: Port all five mass-splitting entry points with native buffer layouts, atomic reservation semantics and the original 64-lane average reduction.
regressions: 61 cases across assignment, splitting, dispatch sizing, scatter and average with 0/1/31/32/33/63/64/65/129 body-count boundaries and 257 hubs
Overflow and zero-capacity pools, clipped counters, static and partially locked bodies, excluded groups, two batches, capacity beyond active body count, shared hub contacts and both contact sides
Exact padding/copied-field protection, duplicate/invalid adjacency and owner rejection, overlapping ranges and missing allocations rejected
Cancellation-sensitive reduction distinguishes the Rust tree order from sequential accumulation; native Metal tests workgroup barriers and reuse
Bounded signed indices avoid an unsigned interval-analysis failure without changing u32 storage/atomic counters; empty non-dispatch stages specialize no-op
differences: No Rust physics or tolerance changes. Nondeterministic hub list and slot allocation order is compared as a legal atomic ordering, with exact totals, capacity, membership and contiguous reservation ownership.

CPU lowering serializes the same per-lane accumulation and tree phases; GPU lowering uses actual workgroup shared memory and barriers. Rust expected averages execute the original shader through khal cooperative CPU dispatch with noalias disabled.
Rust scatters min(requested slots,pool) slots, including a possible unused tail after pool overflow; fixtures preserve its initialized tail mapping instead of silently changing that behavior.

These are isolated stages. Full solver/color scheduling, native frame integration, scene stability, remaining shapes and rigid-body joints are still required. Ascend source lowering does not certify vendor compilation or execution.
